system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
**Buyer-side review — Wattlebridge Holdings.** The Seller’s “[STANDARD]”, “FINAL” and alleged principal-level agreement labels do not establish buyer approval. All positions remain reviewable. The buyer positions below are negotiation recommendations, not assertions of market practice. The underlying DD documents and full SPA have not been supplied.

| Issue | Seller’s position | What the buyer should want | Recommendation and one-line reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001 — General liability cap** | General Warranty Claims capped at 20% of price: **AUD 4.8m**. | A higher general cap, with fundamental/title, tax, specific indemnities and fraud separately addressed. | **Counter at 50% (AUD 12m), subject to diligence and recovery security.** A AUD 4.8m ceiling may leave substantial acquisition risk uninsured and unrecoverable. |
| **SPA-N-002 — De minimis & basket** | Claims must exceed **AUD 25,000**; **AUD 250,000 deductible basket**, with only the excess recoverable. | Lower thresholds; a tipping basket; aggregation of related claims; specified claim categories excluded. | **Propose AUD 10,000 de minimis and AUD 100,000 tipping basket**, disapplying both to fundamental/title, tax, specific indemnities and fraud. The proposed deductible permanently transfers the first AUD 250,000 of qualifying losses to the buyer. |
| **SPA-N-003 — General claims time limit** | Notice within **18 months**; limitations apply to all Claims unless expressly excluded. | At least two full reporting cycles to discover general warranty issues; separate periods for other claim categories. | **Seek 36 months for general warranties**, with timely notified claims surviving resolution and workable notice requirements. Eighteen months may expire before latent issues emerge. |
| **SPA-N-004 — Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title warranties subject to the general cap and time limits. | Separate fundamental warranties covering capacity, authority, ownership, valid issuance and unencumbered transfer of all shares. | **Require a separate cap of at least 100% of price, no thresholds and a longer survival period**, aligned with the agreement’s execution form and applicable NSW limitation rules. Defective ownership threatens the entire investment, not merely operating value. |
| **SPA-N-005 — Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to Claims of every nature; no express fraud exception is supplied. | Express preservation of claims and remedies for Seller fraud and fraudulent misrepresentation, with appropriate attribution of representative conduct. | **Exclude fraud from contractual caps, thresholds, time bars, disclosure/knowledge defences and exclusive-remedy/non-reliance restrictions**, preserving non-excludable rights. The Seller should not obtain contractual protection for fraudulent conduct. |
| **SPA-N-006 — Disclosure scope** | Blanket disclosure of the indexed data room, accounts, registers and publicly searchable corporate records. | Only fair disclosure in sufficient detail to identify the nature and scope of an exception, tied to relevant warranties. | **Reject blanket deemed disclosure; require specific, intelligible disclosures and a frozen, accessible disclosure record.** Merely depositing or referring to documents should not shift unidentified risks to the buyer. |
| **SPA-N-007 — Buyer knowledge qualifier** | No claim for matters known by the buyer or advisers, including anything discoverable from data-room or public material. | No knowledge exclusion; alternatively, tightly defined actual knowledge of named buyer personnel only. | **Delete constructive/imputed knowledge and adviser attribution; preserve indemnity and other agreed claims.** Discoverability is not actual appreciation of a breach or its consequences. |
| **SPA-N-008 — Bluefen consent** | Reasonable endeavours; consent condition satisfied upon delivery of written counterparty consent. No final consent or satisfaction evidence supplied. | Completion conditional on effective consent satisfying clauses 11.2 **and 11.3**, without materially adverse conditions or concessions. | **Require buyer review of the consent and evidence that all associated conditions are satisfied; retain waiver and long-stop termination rights.** Approximately AUD 3.6m revenue—30% of FY26 revenue—is exposed. |
| **SPA-N-009 — Riverlark facility** | Approximately **AUD 3.2m** outstanding; security release to follow Completion. | Debt repaid and security released at Completion through an agreed, enforceable payoff and discharge process. | **Require a current payout letter, direct repayment through funds flow and effective Completion releases; deduct debt once under the price mechanics.** A debt-free/cash-free acquisition must not leave the buyer with outstanding secured debt or an unsecured promise to release it. |
| **SPA-N-010 — Employee bonuses** | **AUD 420,000** conditional Completion bonuses treated as a Seller matter but omitted from funds flow; on-costs unspecified. | Seller bears transaction-triggered bonuses and applicable payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs, with payment obligations verified. | **Expressly allocate the costs to Seller, include them in funds flow or the agreed price adjustment, and obtain a residual indemnity without double counting.** Calling them a Seller matter does not prevent the acquired company inheriting the payment obligation. |
| **SPA-N-011 — Ironquay IP indemnity** | Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; AUD 180,000 remains recorded as open, without payment evidence or confirmatory assignment. | Verified satisfaction of transfer conditions and effective ownership of all relevant project IP, plus protection against residual ownership and infringement consequences. | **Require payment verification and effective assignment/release at Completion; broaden the indemnity beyond the invoice to resulting claims, losses and cure costs.** Paying AUD 180,000 alone may not establish clean IP title or cover consequences of a title defect. |
| **SPA-N-012 — Export/privacy incident** | Preliminary operational matter, said not to be material; access, scope and notification duties remain unresolved. | Prompt investigation, evidence preservation, containment and assessment of privacy, contractual and notification obligations; protection for pre-Completion exposure. | **Require investigation updates, an agreed response plan and a specific indemnity, with Completion protection proportionate to findings.** Uncertainty is not proof of immateriality, but neither does the record establish a confirmed breach or mandatory notification. |
| **SPA-N-013 — Sandbar renewals** | Three AUD 110,000 renewals—**AUD 330,000 aggregate**—characterised as ordinary-course costs. | Assessment together of timing, scope, authority, cancellation rights, accruals and post-Completion benefit. | **Review DD-008 and DD-011 together; restrict new commitments and agree treatment under the price mechanics where justified.** Related renewals cannot be assessed individually, but ordinary future operating costs are not automatically debt-like deductions. |
| **SPA-N-014 — Category separation** | General limitations, exclusive remedies and non-reliance extend to all Claims unless expressly excluded. | Distinct regimes for general warranties, fundamental/title, tax, specific indemnities, price adjustments, covenants and fraud. | **Replace the blanket approach with an express claim-category matrix and precedence provisions.** Otherwise general limitations could unintentionally neutralise specifically negotiated protections and payment obligations. |
| **SPA-N-015 — Title verification** | DD-012’s share register records Harbourglass as holder of 100% of issued shares. | Independent corroboration of ownership, complete capitalisation and absence of options, competing rights or encumbrances. | **Reconcile registers with corporate records, issuance/transfer history and certificates; undertake relevant security searches and obtain releases and Completion title warranties.** The register is important evidence, not conclusive verification of clean title and the entire capital structure. |
| **SPA-N-016 — Tax/IP open terms** | Tax and IP warranties said to be settled under the general regime. | A dedicated pre-Completion tax covenant/indemnity and appropriately scoped tax warranties; robust IP ownership, licensing and infringement protection, separately from Ironquay. | **Reopen both expressly:** seek tax survival through applicable assessment/review periods plus a notice buffer, and separately negotiate adequate IP survival/caps and known-risk indemnities. General 18-month/20% protection is not an adequate default for latent tax liabilities or core technology ownership risk. |

**Drafting caution:** Disclosure should qualify only the warranties expressly agreed—not automatically waive conditions, reduce the price adjustment, or defeat specific indemnities. Likewise, do not convert the lease notification obligation or Mossvale assignment restriction into share-sale consent conditions without supporting contractual language.
=== END ADVICE ===
